object_description: two-story delta-shaped building with excavated courtyards
design_condition: The building is deeply excavated into the sloping site, concentrating the main entrance and parking on the sunny south side while placing interconnected play and garden spaces mainly to the north and west, requiring major topographic interventions and long access routes.

positive.statement: The clear usage units and room groups create a functional construction.
The well-lit rooms resulting from the winding east and southeast facade partly compensate for the low compactness of the volume.
The noise protection is well solved with the low structure and a sound barrier along the highway.
The project shows an interesting basic disposition with great potential for well-organized school operations and clear orientation.
The load transfer works quite economically.

negative.statement: The project entails massive interventions in the existing morphology and places most outdoor areas in the shady north or in difficult-to-reach locations.
Parking on the south side leads to long access roads and brings traffic far into the property.
The planting appears strained and does not follow any recognizable idea.
The completely glazed inner courtyard appears unnecessary and confusing for orientation.
The long corridors result from the large volume and make the organization less compact.
The excavated courtyards and deep excavation require an unnecessarily large amount of gray energy.
The fire protection has deficiencies, including an enclosed stair requirement and a problematic escape-route crossing.
The unfavorable volume and envelope conditions and complex facade constructions lead to rather high investment costs.
